title: Budgets, reachability and the Tau alphabet
summary: The signed Tau alphabet alpha_n = (-1)^n/(n+2)^p spends two budgets, P(p) = sum (2k)^-p and N(p) = sum (2k+1)^-p. This paper records P+N = zeta-1, P-N = 1-eta and the closed forms (PROVED in Lean); that the alphabet totals 1-ln2 = +0.30685..., not its negative; Brown's criterion a_k <= T_{k+1} for every k, giving the exact reachable set, with the brief's single condition REFUTED in Lean; the census measure(S_1) = 2^(n_min-1) T_{n_min}; the thresholds pN < pP < p* < q; and the parity lock: every take at a positive target is even, so all gaps are even and >= 2. Not the twin prime conjecture.
recipe_md:
All commands run from inside `research/publish/003-budgets-reachability-tau`.

1. `./check.sh --all` -- elaborates the Lean 4 + Mathlib development. Expected: exit 0, one `[check] OK <file>` line per file; observed all five OK, about 11 minutes. Needs elan at `$LEAN_PREFIX/elan` and Mathlib4 at `$LEAN_PREFIX/mathlib4`, toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2`.
2. `python3 reachable.py` -- the exact reachable-set theory. Expected: exit 0, 70 checks, `ALL 70 CHECKS PASS`. WARNING: as published the script exits 1 immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rh41'` (it imports `rh41.digitword`); with an importable `rh41` package built from the published `digitword.py` on `PYTHONPATH`, the observed run gives 70/70. The folder README's claim that everything needed is in the folder is false for the Python layer.
3. `python3 helix_zeta.py` -- the budget/criterion investigation. Expected: exit 0, 80 checks, `ALL 80 CHECKS PASS`; same `rh41.digitword` import requirement.
